record.paper_title: Solutions to Some Open Problems from Slaney
record.original_question: Start with the positive logic TW+[Ax L, AxTO] and adjoin a fusion connective ◦ governed by the two-way residuation rule (Resid): `(A ◦ B) → C` if and only if `A → (B → C)`. Is this extension conservative over the original language containing only →, ∧, and ∨; that is, after adding (Resid), does the resulting theory prove no new theorems whose formulas involve only →, ∧, and ∨?

evidence.quote: 3. Is the addition of fusion a conservative extension of the positive logic TW+[Ax L, AxTO]? That is, does the addition of (Resid) to TW+[Ax L, AxTO] imply no new theorems involving only h→, ∧, ∨i?
Our second theorem implies both a negative answer to (3) and a positive answer to (4). Theorem 2. (AxK) and (AxC) are provable in TW+[Ax L, AxTO] + (Resid).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the positive relevance logic TW+ (the positive fragment of the contraction-less relevance logic TW, with connectives →, ∧, ∨ and the usual axioms and rules: identity A→A; prefixing (B→C)→((A→B)→(A→C)); suffixing (A→B)→((B→C)→(A→C)); the standard lattice axioms for ∧ and ∨ together with distribution A∧(B∨C)→(A∧B)∨(A∧C); the rules of modus ponens and adjunction), augmented with the two axioms:
  (Ax L)  ((A→B)∧(C→D)) → ((A∧C) → (B∧D)),
  (Ax TO) ((A→B)∧(C→D)) → ((A∨C) → (B∨D)).

Now extend the language with a binary fusion connective ◦ governed by the two-way residuation rule
  (Resid)  ⊢ (A ◦ B) → C   if and only if   ⊢ A → (B → C).

Question: Is the resulting logic TW+[Ax L, Ax TO] + (Resid) a conservative extension of TW+[Ax L, Ax TO] over the original language {→, ∧, ∨}? That is, does every theorem of the extended system whose formula contains only →, ∧, and ∨ already belong to TW+[Ax L, Ax TO]?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved in the negative. It has been shown that adding the residuation rule (Resid) for fusion to TW+[Ax L, Ax TO] allows derivation of the axioms (AxK) A→(B→A) and (AxC) (A→(B→C))→(B→(A→C)), which are not theorems of the original positive logic. Hence the extension is not conservative.

status_evidence.title: Solutions to Some Open Problems from Slaney (zbMATH)
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 2. (AxK) and (AxC) are provable in TW+[Ax L, AxTO] + (Resid). ... implies a negative answer to (3).
status_evidence.claim: The extension by fusion with residuation proves (AxK) and (AxC), giving a negative answer to the conservativity question.
